To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

human fetal liver mesenchymal stromal cells prolonged survival and enhanced engraftment when cotransplanted into NOD/Shi-SCID/IL-2 receptor γ(null) mice with umbilical cord hematopoietic progenitor cells.
hFL-MSC engrafted in the marrow, spleen, and peripheral blood of NOG mice and enhanced human cell engrafts in irradiated NOGS mice.
the number of cotranplanted hFL-MSC is an important factor to enhance the engraftment level of human cells in NOG mice in our in vivo model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of MSCs on HSC repopulation and survival in NOG mice.
the role of human fetal liver-MSCs in HSC engrafts in NOG mice.
the effect of hFL-MCSs on engraftment and survival of UCB CD34+ HSCs in NOG mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of MSCs on HSC engraftsment is dose-dependent and that the dose used in this study was insufficient to increase HSC repopulation in vivo.
hFL-MSC transplantation did not significantly enhance the repopulating ability of UCB CD34+ cells in irradiated NOGs in this study.
cotransplantation with hFL-MSC may be a useful strategy in the future for improving engraftment efficiency and reducing the number of transplanted HSCs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
human FL-MSCs are not capable of increasing the number of repopulating human HSCs in NOG mice in our in vitro system.
hFL-MSC transplantation is not a sufficient strategy for improving HSC engrafts in NOG mice.
human fetal liver-derived hFL-MSC can be a potential candidate for the support of hematopoietically stem cell repopulating.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hFL-MSC may be a potential cell source for the development of a cellular therapy for hematopoietic disorders.
human fetal liver-derived cells have the potential to support engraftment, but the number of cells required to achieve a positive effect on engraftment is not yet clear.

hFL-MSC transplantation is a safe procedure and that the use of hFL-MCSs as a feeder layer in ex vivo culture of human hematopoietic progenitor cells is a promising strategy for improving engraftment.
